content.title: About
content.content: Sweet pickled peppers are whole or sliced sweet bell peppers that have been cured in a brine of vinegar, salt, spices, and sometimes sugar. The peppers retain a crisp texture while acquiring a tangy‑sweet flavor typical of traditional pickles.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Sweet bell peppers are very high in vitamin C – one medium pepper provides over 100 % of the daily requirement.
Pickling can preserve peppers for up to a year when stored properly.
Traditional recipes often include coriander, mustard seeds, garlic, and bay leaf for extra aroma.
Sweet pickled peppers are popular in Mediterranean, Asian, and Latin American cuisines.
They are used in salads, sandwiches, pizza, and as a garnish for meat dishes.

items.title: Rich in vitamin C
items.content: Vitamin C is a powerful antioxidant that supports immunity and collagen synthesis.

items.title: Contains antioxidants
items.content: Carotenoids and polyphenols in peppers help combat free radicals.

items.title: Low‑calorie food
items.content: A cup of pickled peppers contains about 30 kcal, making it a diet‑friendly snack.

items.title: Supports digestion
items.content: The fiber in peppers promotes healthy bowel function.

items.title: Provides vitamin B6
items.content: Vitamin B6 is involved in protein metabolism and neurotransmitter synthesis.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: Pickled foods can be high in salt; people with hypertension should monitor portion size.

items.title: Pepper allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to capsaicin or other pepper components.

items.title: Acidity
items.content: The vinegar’s acidity may irritate the stomach in people with gastritis or ulcers.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Sweet pickled peppers can be enjoyed as a snack, added to salads, sandwiches, pasta, pizza, omelets, or used as a garnish for meat and fish. Before serving, they are often drained of excess brine.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the opened jar in the refrigerator with the lid tightly sealed. Properly stored, the product remains good for 3‑6 months. Discard any peppers that show mold, off‑smells, or discoloration.
